home.title: Farm layout and production plan for every level
home.intro: For every player level: where to place the buildings in production blocks, what to do at each login and what to produce. Each recommendation is for a player who bought nothing beyond the level (level defaults, no mastery, barn and silo not set), laid out on the starting farm area.
home.notPlacedNote: From about level 36 on, not every block fits on the starting farm area; the level cards mark them. Which farm plots to unlock comes in a later version.

how.title: How it works
how.intro: The site is computed in four steps from public game data. The same steps run on your own computer with your own farm.
how.graphText: Locations, goods and recipes from the Hay Day Wiki become a weighted directed graph: what each building needs and where its goods go.
how.blocksText: Buildings that trade a lot of goods form a named production block around an anchor building, with its own fields for the crops it uses.
how.layoutText: The blocks are packed onto the farm area, the strongest goods flows close together, and paths connect them to the barn and the silo.
how.planText: A linear program chooses what to produce with the level's buildings, slots and fields, and turns it into actions for each login.

usage.title: Usage
usage.intro: The recommendations here use level defaults. For a plan of your own farm, run the tools locally (Python 3.14).
usage.installText: Clone the repository and install the requirements in a virtual environment.
usage.wizardText: Answer a few questions about your level, buildings and slots; the answers go into config/player.json.
usage.mapText: Open tools/farm_map_editor.html in a browser and measure your farm from a screenshot. Optional: without it the starting farm area is used.
usage.runText: One command makes the graph, the farm layout, the production plan and the combined plan in output/.
